"Your table's waiting," she says.|"Your regulars asked after you," says the landlady, which is either flattering or a warning. Upstairs the lamps are lit.} Work the room {You button the jacket and go up. It fits a little better than last time.|You take your jacket from its peg and climb the stair into the lamplight.|Your regulars wave you over before you've reached the top of the stair.} Not tonight {"Next week, then," she says, and the jacket goes back on its peg.|She shrugs and chalks a line through tonight beside your name.|"They'll miss you," she says, and it sounds like the truth and the bill at once.}
